mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The alternation of polyp and medusa illustrated by Obelia; B. The principal mineral of a stony coral skeleton; C. The cnidarian commonly called Portuguese man-of-war. List II: 1. Metagenesis; 2. Calcium carbonate; 3. Physalia. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–2, C–3. Obelia alternates asexual polyp reproduction with the sexual medusa stage. Reef-forming corals deposit calcium carbonate skeletons. Physalia is a colonial cnidarian rather than a true fish.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The cnidarian commonly called Portuguese man-of-war; B. The locomotory structures of ctenophores; C. The habitat restriction of ctenophores in the textbook account. List II: 1. Exclusively marine; 2. Physalia; 3. Eight rows of ciliated comb plates. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–3, C–1. Physalia is a colonial cnidarian rather than a true fish. Coordinated beating of comb plates moves ctenophores through water. Comb jellies are marine animals.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The habitat restriction of ctenophores in the textbook account; B. The ctenophore genus among these examples; C. The organs of osmoregulation and excretion in flatworms. List II: 1. Flame-cell systems; 2. Pleurobrachia; 3. Exclusively marine. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–2, C–1. Comb jellies are marine animals. Pleurobrachia is a comb jelly; Physalia is a cnidarian. Flame cells form part of protonephridial systems.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The organs of osmoregulation and excretion in flatworms; B. The flatworm renowned for regeneration; C. The genus commonly called tapeworm. List II: 1. Planaria; 2. Flame-cell systems; 3. Taenia. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–1, C–3. Flame cells form part of protonephridial systems. Planarians can regenerate missing body regions from fragments. Taenia is an endoparasitic cestode or tapeworm.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The genus commonly called tapeworm; B. The genus commonly called liver fluke; C. The main function of hooks and suckers in parasitic flatworms. List II: 1. Taenia; 2. Attachment to the host; 3. Fasciola. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–3, C–2. Taenia is an endoparasitic cestode or tapeworm. Fasciola is a parasitic flatworm associated with the liver and bile ducts. Attachment structures prevent displacement within the host.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The main function of hooks and suckers in parasitic flatworms; B. The digestive tract condition typical of roundworms; C. The sexual organisation typical of Ascaris. List II: 1. Complete with mouth and anus; 2. Separate male and female individuals; 3. Attachment to the host. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–1, C–2. Attachment structures prevent displacement within the host. Roundworms have an alimentary canal with two openings. Ascaris is dioecious and shows sexual dimorphism.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The sexual organisation typical of Ascaris; B. The usual relative size of female and male Ascaris; C. The nematode genus associated with lymphatic filariasis. List II: 1. Separate male and female individuals; 2. Female larger than male; 3. Wuchereria. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–2, C–3. Ascaris is dioecious and shows sexual dimorphism. Female Ascaris generally have a larger body than males. Wuchereria can infect lymphatic vessels and cause elephantiasis.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The nematode genus associated with lymphatic filariasis; B. The roundworm commonly known as hookworm; C. The excretory structures characteristic of annelids. List II: 1. Nephridia; 2. Wuchereria; 3. Ancylostoma. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–3, C–1. Wuchereria can infect lymphatic vessels and cause elephantiasis. Ancylostoma attaches to the intestinal mucosa and feeds on blood. Annelid nephridia remove wastes and regulate fluid balance.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The excretory structures characteristic of annelids; B. The circulatory system generally described for annelids; C. The lateral swimming appendages of Nereis. List II: 1. Parapodia; 2. Closed; 3. Nephridia. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–2, C–1. Annelid nephridia remove wastes and regulate fluid balance. Blood circulates within vessels in the typical annelid system. Parapodia are paired lateral outgrowths used in locomotion.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The lateral swimming appendages of Nereis; B. The annelid genus commonly called a leech; C. The annelid with separate sexes among these textbook examples. List II: 1. Hirudinaria; 2. Parapodia; 3. Nereis. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–1, C–3. Parapodia are paired lateral outgrowths used in locomotion. Hirudinaria is a leech with an annelid segmented body. Nereis is dioecious, whereas earthworms and many leeches are hermaphroditic.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The annelid with separate sexes among these textbook examples; B. The largest animal phylum by number of described species; C. The main structural polysaccharide of the arthropod exoskeleton. List II: 1. Chitin; 2. Arthropoda; 3. Nereis. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–2, C–1. Nereis is dioecious, whereas earthworms and many leeches are hermaphroditic. Arthropods, especially insects, account for the greatest described animal diversity. A chitin-containing cuticle forms the arthropod exoskeleton.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The main structural polysaccharide of the arthropod exoskeleton; B. The excretory tubules typical of insects; C. The respiratory organs characteristic of a terrestrial insect. List II: 1. Malpighian tubules; 2. Chitin; 3. Tracheae. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–1, C–3. A chitin-containing cuticle forms the arthropod exoskeleton. Malpighian tubules remove wastes from haemolymph into the gut. A branching tracheal network delivers gases directly to tissues.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The respiratory organs characteristic of a terrestrial insect; B. The arthropod commonly called a living fossil in standard; C. The insect genus used in commercial silk production. List II: 1. Tracheae; 2. Bombyx; 3. Limulus. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–3, C–2. A branching tracheal network delivers gases directly to tissues. The horseshoe crab Limulus is cited as a living fossil. Bombyx mori larvae produce silk cocoons.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The insect genus used in commercial silk production; B. The second largest animal phylum in the textbook account; C. The molluscan fold covering the visceral mass. List II: 1. Mollusca; 2. Mantle; 3. Bombyx. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–1, C–2. Bombyx mori larvae produce silk cocoons. Molluscs rank after arthropods in described species diversity in this account. The mantle covers the visceral mass and commonly secretes the shell.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The molluscan fold covering the visceral mass; B. The rasping feeding organ found in most molluscs; C. The molluscan genus commonly called devil fish. List II: 1. Mantle; 2. Radula; 3. Octopus. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–2, C–3. The mantle covers the visceral mass and commonly secretes the shell. The radula bears rows of teeth; bivalves are an important exception. Octopus is a cephalopod mollusc, not a fish.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The molluscan genus commonly called devil fish; B. The mollusc associated with pearl production; C. The mollusc commonly called sea hare. List II: 1. Aplysia; 2. Octopus; 3. Pinctada. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–3, C–1. Octopus is a cephalopod mollusc, not a fish. Pearl oysters of Pinctada can deposit nacre around an irritant. Aplysia is a gastropod mollusc.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The mollusc commonly called sea hare; B. The body symmetry of an adult starfish; C. The body symmetry of a typical echinoderm larva. List II: 1. Bilateral; 2. Radial, usually pentamerous; 3. Aplysia. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–2, C–1. Aplysia is a gastropod mollusc. Adult echinoderms are radially organised, commonly around five sectors. Echinoderm larvae are bilateral even though adults are radial.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The body symmetry of a typical echinoderm larva; B. The skeletal material of echinoderm ossicles; C. The locomotory extensions operated by the water vascular system. List II: 1. Calcium carbonate; 2. Bilateral; 3. Tube feet. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–1, C–3. Echinoderm larvae are bilateral even though adults are radial. Calcareous ossicles form the echinoderm endoskeleton. Hydraulically operated tube feet participate in locomotion and other functions.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The locomotory extensions operated by the water vascular system; B. The echinoderm commonly called brittle star; C. The habitat of all living echinoderms. List II: 1. Tube feet; 2. Marine; 3. Ophiura. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–3, C–2. Hydraulically operated tube feet participate in locomotion and other functions. Ophiura has slender flexible arms characteristic of brittle stars. Echinoderms are exclusively marine.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The habitat of all living echinoderms; B. The three body regions of Balanoglossus; C. The excretory structure described for hemichordates. List II: 1. Proboscis, collar and trunk; 2. Proboscis gland; 3. Marine. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–1, C–2. Echinoderms are exclusively marine. Hemichordates have a proboscis-collar-trunk body plan. The proboscis gland participates in excretion in hemichordates.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The excretory structure described for hemichordates; B. The embryonic origin of the notochord; C. The nerve cord arrangement characteristic of chordates. List II: 1. Proboscis gland; 2. Mesoderm; 3. Dorsal and hollow. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–2, C–3. The proboscis gland participates in excretion in hemichordates. The notochord is a mesodermal supporting rod. A dorsal hollow neural tube is a key chordate feature.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The nerve cord arrangement characteristic of chordates; B. The restriction of the notochord in Urochordata; C. The notochord condition in Cephalochordata. List II: 1. Extends from head to tail throughout life; 2. Dorsal and hollow; 3. To the larval tail. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–3, C–1. A dorsal hollow neural tube is a key chordate feature. Tunicate larvae have a tail notochord that is lost during metamorphosis in typical forms. Branchiostoma retains a longitudinal notochord as an adult.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The notochord condition in Cephalochordata; B. The representative cephalochordate genus; C. The mouth of a cyclostome. List II: 1. Circular and jawless; 2. Branchiostoma; 3. Extends from head to tail throughout life. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–2, C–1. Branchiostoma retains a longitudinal notochord as an adult. Branchiostoma, also called Amphioxus, is a lancelet. Cyclostomes have a circular sucking mouth without jaws.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The mouth of a cyclostome; B. The skeleton characteristic of Chondrichthyes; C. The scale type characteristic of sharks. List II: 1. Cartilaginous; 2. Circular and jawless; 3. Placoid. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–1, C–3. Cyclostomes have a circular sucking mouth without jaws. Cartilaginous fishes have a cartilage-based endoskeleton. Placoid scales are tooth-like dermal structures.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The scale type characteristic of sharks; B. The buoyancy organ generally absent in cartilaginous fishes; C. The flap covering the gills in most bony fishes. List II: 1. Placoid; 2. Operculum; 3. Air bladder. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–3, C–2. Placoid scales are tooth-like dermal structures. Sharks lack the air bladder present in many bony fishes. An operculum covers the gill chamber in most Osteichthyes.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The flap covering the gills in most bony fishes; B. The number of chambers in a typical fish heart; C. The bony fish commonly called seahorse. List II: 1. Two; 2. Hippocampus; 3. Operculum. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–1, C–2. An operculum covers the gill chamber in most Osteichthyes. A fish heart has one atrium and one ventricle. Hippocampus is a marine bony fish.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The bony fish commonly called seahorse; B. The cartilaginous fish commonly called electric ray; C. The number of heart chambers typical of amphibians. List II: 1. Hippocampus; 2. Torpedo; 3. Three. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–2, C–3. Hippocampus is a marine bony fish. Torpedo possesses electric organs. Amphibians generally have two atria and one ventricle.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The number of heart chambers typical of amphibians; B. The usual skin covering of amphibians; C. The class containing Salamandra and Ichthyophis. List II: 1. Amphibia; 2. Three; 3. Moist glandular skin without scales. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–3, C–1. Amphibians generally have two atria and one ventricle. Amphibian skin is usually moist and involved in gas exchange. Salamanders and limbless caecilians are amphibians.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The class containing Salamandra and Ichthyophis; B. The skin covering typical of reptiles; C. The reptile group with a four-chambered heart. List II: 1. Crocodilians; 2. Dry cornified scales or scutes; 3. Amphibia. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–2, C–1. Salamanders and limbless caecilians are amphibians. Keratinised scales help reptiles limit water loss. Crocodilians have four heart chambers, unlike the usual textbook reptilian pattern.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The reptile group with a four-chambered heart; B. The reptile commonly called garden lizard; C. The poisonous snake genus commonly called krait. List II: 1. Calotes; 2. Crocodilians; 3. Bungarus. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–1, C–3. Crocodilians have four heart chambers, unlike the usual textbook reptilian pattern. Calotes is the garden lizard. Bungarus includes kraits, which are venomous snakes.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The poisonous snake genus commonly called krait; B. The skeletal feature helping reduce body mass in many birds; C. The forelimb modification characteristic of birds. List II: 1. Bungarus; 2. Wings; 3. Pneumatic bones. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–3, C–2. Bungarus includes kraits, which are venomous snakes. Air spaces within many bones reduce mass while preserving support. Bird forelimbs are modified as wings, even in species unable to fly.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The forelimb modification characteristic of birds; B. The number of chambers in a bird's heart; C. The temperature-regulation category shared by birds and mammals. List II: 1. Four; 2. Endothermy; 3. Wings. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–1, C–2. Bird forelimbs are modified as wings, even in species unable to fly. Two atria and two ventricles separate oxygenated and deoxygenated blood. Birds and mammals produce substantial metabolic heat and regulate body temperature.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The temperature-regulation category shared by birds and mammals; B. The flightless bird genus Struthio; C. The gland defining the mammalian feeding adaptation for young. List II: 1. Endothermy; 2. Ostrich; 3. Mammary gland. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–2, C–3. Birds and mammals produce substantial metabolic heat and regulate body temperature. Struthio is the ostrich. Mammary glands secrete milk to nourish offspring.
mcqs.subject: Biology

chapters.name: Morphology of Flowering Plants

mcqs.question: Prop roots occur in:
mcqs.explanation: Banyan branches produce pillar-like prop roots for support.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: A potato tuber is a modified:
mcqs.explanation: Its eyes are axillary buds, showing that potato is a stem tuber.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The edible part of a coconut is mainly the:
mcqs.explanation: Coconut water and kernel are liquid and solid endosperm, respectively.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: In a hypogynous flower, the ovary is:
mcqs.explanation: Other floral whorls arise below the ovary in hypogynous flowers.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Valvate aestivation occurs when sepals or petals:
options: Touch at the margins without overlapping
mcqs.explanation: Valvate members meet at their edges but do not overlap.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The fruit of pea is classified as a:
mcqs.explanation: Pea develops a dry dehiscent legume from a monocarpellary ovary.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The embryonic structure giving rise to the primary root is:
mcqs.explanation: The radicle elongates into the primary root during germination.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The root system characteristic of mustard is:
mcqs.explanation: The primary root persists and gives off lateral branches in mustard.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The root system characteristic of wheat is:
mcqs.explanation: Roots arising near the stem base replace the short-lived primary root in wheat.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Roots arising from plant parts other than the radicle is:
mcqs.explanation: Adventitious roots may arise from stems, nodes or leaves.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The protective structure covering the growing root apex is:
mcqs.explanation: The root cap protects delicate apical cells as the root pushes through soil.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The root region with actively dividing cells is:
mcqs.explanation: The apical meristem supplies new cells for root growth.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The root region chiefly responsible for increase in length through cell enlargement is:
mcqs.explanation: Cells enlarge rapidly in the elongation zone behind the meristem.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The root zone commonly bearing root hairs is:
mcqs.explanation: Differentiated epidermal cells develop root hairs in the maturation zone.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The main function of root hairs is:
options: Conduct photosynthesis as the main organ
mcqs.explanation: Root hairs enlarge contact with soil water and dissolved minerals.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The root modification storing food in carrot is:
mcqs.explanation: Carrot's swollen taproot stores reserve nutrients.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The food-storing root of sweet potato is:
mcqs.explanation: Sweet potato stores food in swollen adventitious roots, unlike potato stem tubers.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The supporting roots arising from lower stem nodes of maize is:
mcqs.explanation: Maize stilt roots grow obliquely from lower nodes into the soil.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The upward-growing respiratory roots in Rhizophora is:
mcqs.explanation: Pneumatophores help gas exchange in waterlogged, oxygen-poor soil.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The embryonic structure developing into the shoot is:
mcqs.explanation: The plumule forms the young shoot system.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The point on a stem where a leaf arises is:
mcqs.explanation: Nodes are the sites of leaf and often bud attachment.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The stem region between successive nodes is:
mcqs.explanation: Internodes separate adjacent nodes.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The bud found in the angle between a leaf and stem is:
mcqs.explanation: An axillary bud occurs in the leaf axil and may form a branch or flower.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The diagnostic feature identifying potato as a stem tuber is:
options: Presence of root hairs on each eye
mcqs.explanation: Potato eyes are nodes with buds, indicating stem origin.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The underground stem modification of ginger is:
mcqs.explanation: Ginger is a horizontal underground stem with nodes, buds and scale leaves.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The storage structure of onion is:
mcqs.explanation: An onion bulb has a short stem surrounded by fleshy leaf bases.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The climbing stem modification of grapevine is:
mcqs.explanation: Grapevine tendrils are stem-derived climbing structures.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The protective stem modification of Citrus is:
mcqs.explanation: Citrus thorns are modified axillary shoots.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The flattened photosynthetic stem of Opuntia is:
mcqs.explanation: Opuntia stems conduct photosynthesis while leaves are reduced to spines.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The underground condensed stem of Colocasia is:
mcqs.explanation: A corm is a short swollen underground stem.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The horizontal creeping stem rooting at nodes in lawn grass is:
mcqs.explanation: Runners spread along the surface and establish new plants at nodes.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The one-internode vegetative propagule characteristic of Pistia is:
mcqs.explanation: An offset is a short lateral branch typical of some floating aquatic plants.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The leaf part attaching it to the stem is:
mcqs.explanation: The leaf base joins the leaf to the stem.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The stalk of a typical petiolate leaf is:
mcqs.explanation: A petiole connects the lamina with the leaf base.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The expanded blade of a leaf is:
mcqs.explanation: The lamina is the main flattened photosynthetic region.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The swollen leaf base common in legumes is:
mcqs.explanation: A pulvinus is a swollen leaf base often involved in leaf movements.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The small lateral appendages at the leaf base in a stipulate leaf is:
mcqs.explanation: Stipules flank the leaf base; not all leaves possess them.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The net-like arrangement of veins in a leaf is:
mcqs.explanation: Reticulate veins form an interconnected network.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The venation commonly found in grass leaves is:
mcqs.explanation: Monocot grasses commonly have veins running broadly parallel.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The leaf type in which incisions reach the midrib and separate leaflets is:
mcqs.explanation: Deep incisions separating individual leaflets produce a compound leaf.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The feature usually present at the base of a whole leaf but absent at leaflet bases is:
mcqs.explanation: An axillary bud distinguishes a leaf from an individual leaflet.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The compound leaf type of neem is:
mcqs.explanation: Neem leaflets are arranged along a common rachis.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The compound leaf type of silk cotton is:
mcqs.explanation: Silk cotton leaflets radiate from one point.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The common axis bearing leaflets in a pinnate leaf is:
mcqs.explanation: The rachis is the extended leaf axis carrying leaflets.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The arrangement with one leaf at each node is:
mcqs.explanation: Alternate leaves arise singly at successive nodes.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The arrangement with two leaves at each node is:
options: Whorled with three or more leaves
mcqs.explanation: Opposite leaves occur in pairs at a node.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The arrangement with more than two leaves at a node is:
mcqs.explanation: A whorl contains three or more leaves around the same node.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The leaf arrangement illustrated by Alstonia is:
mcqs.explanation: Alstonia commonly bears a whorl of leaves at each node.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The leaf arrangement illustrated by guava is:
mcqs.explanation: Guava leaves are arranged in opposite pairs.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The climbing modification of pea leaflets is:
mcqs.explanation: Pea leaflets may be modified into tendrils for support.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The main protective leaf modification in cactus is:
mcqs.explanation: Cactus leaves are reduced to spines, limiting water loss and providing defence.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The photosynthetic flattened petiole of Australian Acacia is:
mcqs.explanation: A phyllode is a modified petiole, whereas a phylloclade is stem-derived.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The insect-trapping modification of Nepenthes is:
mcqs.explanation: The pitcher is derived from the leaf and traps small animals.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The arrangement of flowers on a floral axis is:
mcqs.explanation: Inflorescence describes the pattern of flowers on the reproductive axis.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The inflorescence with an indefinitely growing main axis is:
mcqs.explanation: In racemose inflorescences the main axis continues growth.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The inflorescence whose main axis ends in a flower is:
mcqs.explanation: A terminal flower limits main-axis growth in a cyme.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The usual sequence of flower age along a racemose axis is:
mcqs.explanation: Acropetal succession places younger flowers toward the apex.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The usual sequence of flower age in a simple cyme is:
options: Older terminal, younger toward the base
mcqs.explanation: Basipetal succession follows termination of the main axis by an older flower.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The stalk of an individual flower is:
mcqs.explanation: The pedicel supports an individual flower.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The swollen floral axis bearing the floral whorls is:
mcqs.explanation: Floral organs arise on the thalamus or receptacle.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The outermost floral whorl in a typical complete flower is:
mcqs.explanation: The calyx consists of sepals outside the petals.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The floral whorl made of petals is:
mcqs.explanation: Petals collectively form the corolla.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The male reproductive whorl of a flower is:
mcqs.explanation: The androecium consists of stamens.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The female reproductive whorl of a flower is:
mcqs.explanation: The gynoecium is composed of one or more carpels.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The symmetry of a flower divisible into similar halves in many vertical planes is:
mcqs.explanation: Actinomorphic flowers show radial symmetry about their central axis.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The symmetry of a pea flower is:
mcqs.explanation: A pea flower can be divided into equivalent halves in one principal vertical plane.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The symmetry of a Canna flower is:
mcqs.explanation: Canna flowers cannot be divided into two equal halves by a vertical plane.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: A flower containing both stamens and carpels is:
mcqs.explanation: A bisexual flower has both male and female reproductive organs.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: A flower subtended by a bract is:
mcqs.explanation: Bracteate means a bract occurs at the base of the flower or its stalk.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The condition in which sepals are fused is:
mcqs.explanation: Gamosepalous refers to union among sepals.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The condition in which petals are free is:
mcqs.explanation: Polypetalous flowers have separate petals.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The aestivation in which each petal overlaps the next in one direction is:
mcqs.explanation: Twisted aestivation produces regular overlap in a consistent direction.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The aestivation with irregular petal overlap and no fixed direction is:
mcqs.explanation: Imbricate petals overlap irregularly.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The aestivation characteristic of pea is:
mcqs.explanation: The standard overlaps the wings, which overlap the keel petals.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The large posterior petal of a papilionaceous corolla is:
mcqs.explanation: The standard or vexillum is the largest petal in the pea-type corolla.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The ovary position in an epigynous flower is:
mcqs.explanation: Other floral parts arise above the ovary in epigynous flowers.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The stalk of a stamen is:
mcqs.explanation: The filament supports the pollen-bearing anther.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The pollen-producing part of a stamen is:
mcqs.explanation: Pollen develops in the microsporangia of the anther.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The attachment of stamens to petals is:
mcqs.explanation: Epipetalous stamens are attached to petals, as in brinjal.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The condition with staminal filaments united into one bundle is:
mcqs.explanation: Monadelphous filaments form one bundle, as in China rose.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The condition with staminal filaments united into two bundles is:
mcqs.explanation: Pea shows two bundles, commonly a 9+1 arrangement.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The sterile stamen of a flower is:
mcqs.explanation: A staminode is a nonfunctional or sterile stamen.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The pollen-receptive part of a carpel is:
mcqs.explanation: The stigma receives pollen during pollination.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The slender connection between stigma and ovary is:
mcqs.explanation: The style connects the stigma to the ovary.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The gynoecium with free carpels is:
mcqs.explanation: Apocarpous carpels remain separate, as in lotus.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The gynoecium with fused carpels is:
mcqs.explanation: Carpels are united in a syncarpous gynoecium, as in tomato.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The placentation of pea is:
mcqs.explanation: Ovules occur along the ventral suture of the single carpel.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The placentation of tomato is:
mcqs.explanation: Ovules attach to a central axis in a multilocular ovary.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The placentation of mustard is:
mcqs.explanation: Ovules arise from the inner ovary wall; a false septum may divide the chamber.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The placentation of Dianthus is:
mcqs.explanation: Ovules attach to a free central axis without septa dividing the ovary.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The placentation of sunflower is:
mcqs.explanation: The ovule is attached near the base of the unilocular ovary.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The fruit wall formed from the ovary wall is:
mcqs.explanation: The pericarp may differentiate into outer, middle and inner layers.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The hard stony inner layer of a mango fruit is:
mcqs.explanation: The lignified endocarp surrounds the seed in a drupe.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The seed attachment scar is:
mcqs.explanation: The hilum marks the former attachment of the funicle.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The small pore in a seed coat is:
mcqs.explanation: The micropyle permits water and gas entry during germination.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: The shield-shaped cotyledon of a grass embryo is:
mcqs.explanation: The scutellum is the single cotyledon of the grass embryo.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The embryonic structure giving rise to the primary root: Radicle. II. The root system characteristic of mustard: Taproot system. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is correct. The radicle elongates into the primary root during germination. The primary root persists and gives off lateral branches in mustard.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The root system characteristic of wheat: Only coralloid roots. II. Roots arising from plant parts other than the radicle: Root caps. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is incorrect. Roots arising near the stem base replace the short-lived primary root in wheat. Adventitious roots may arise from stems, nodes or leaves.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The protective structure covering the growing root apex: Root cap. II. The root region with actively dividing cells: Mature root-hair zone only. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is incorrect. The root cap protects delicate apical cells as the root pushes through soil. The apical meristem supplies new cells for root growth.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The root region chiefly responsible for increase in length through cell enlargement: Region of maturation. II. The root zone commonly bearing root hairs: Region of maturation. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is correct. Cells enlarge rapidly in the elongation zone behind the meristem. Differentiated epidermal cells develop root hairs in the maturation zone.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The main function of root hairs: Conduct photosynthesis as the main organ. II. The root modification storing food in carrot: Storage taproot. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is correct. Root hairs enlarge contact with soil water and dissolved minerals. Carrot's swollen taproot stores reserve nutrients.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The food-storing root of sweet potato: Tuberous adventitious root. II. The supporting roots arising from lower stem nodes of maize: Prop roots descending from branches. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is incorrect. Sweet potato stores food in swollen adventitious roots, unlike potato stem tubers. Maize stilt roots grow obliquely from lower nodes into the soil.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The upward-growing respiratory roots in Rhizophora: Storage taproots. II. The embryonic structure developing into the shoot: Root cap. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is incorrect. Pneumatophores help gas exchange in waterlogged, oxygen-poor soil. The plumule forms the young shoot system.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The point on a stem where a leaf arises: Node. II. The stem region between successive nodes: Internode. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is correct. Nodes are the sites of leaf and often bud attachment. Internodes separate adjacent nodes.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The bud found in the angle between a leaf and stem: Axillary bud. II. The diagnostic feature identifying potato as a stem tuber: Absence of all nodes. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is incorrect. An axillary bud occurs in the leaf axil and may form a branch or flower. Potato eyes are nodes with buds, indicating stem origin.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The underground stem modification of ginger: Rhizome. II. The storage structure of onion: Bulb. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is correct. Ginger is a horizontal underground stem with nodes, buds and scale leaves. An onion bulb has a short stem surrounded by fleshy leaf bases.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The climbing stem modification of grapevine: Pneumatophore. II. The protective stem modification of Citrus: Thorn. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is correct. Grapevine tendrils are stem-derived climbing structures. Citrus thorns are modified axillary shoots.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The flattened photosynthetic stem of Opuntia: Sepal. II. The underground condensed stem of Colocasia: Bulb made only of leaves. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is incorrect. Opuntia stems conduct photosynthesis while leaves are reduced to spines. A corm is a short swollen underground stem.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The horizontal creeping stem rooting at nodes in lawn grass: Corm. II. The one-internode vegetative propagule characteristic of Pistia: Rhizome. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is incorrect. Runners spread along the surface and establish new plants at nodes. An offset is a short lateral branch typical of some floating aquatic plants.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The leaf part attaching it to the stem: Leaf apex. II. The stalk of a typical petiolate leaf: Petiole. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is correct. The leaf base joins the leaf to the stem. A petiole connects the lamina with the leaf base.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The expanded blade of a leaf: Lamina. II. The swollen leaf base common in legumes: Pulvinus. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is correct. The lamina is the main flattened photosynthetic region. A pulvinus is a swollen leaf base often involved in leaf movements.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The small lateral appendages at the leaf base in a stipulate leaf: Stipules. II. The net-like arrangement of veins in a leaf: Dichotomous branching of roots. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is incorrect. Stipules flank the leaf base; not all leaves possess them. Reticulate veins form an interconnected network.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The venation commonly found in grass leaves: Parallel venation. II. The leaf type in which incisions reach the midrib and separate leaflets: Phylloclade. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is incorrect. Monocot grasses commonly have veins running broadly parallel. Deep incisions separating individual leaflets produce a compound leaf.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The feature usually present at the base of a whole leaf but absent at leaflet bases: Lamina tissue. II. The compound leaf type of neem: Palmately compound. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is incorrect. An axillary bud distinguishes a leaf from an individual leaflet. Neem leaflets are arranged along a common rachis.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The compound leaf type of silk cotton: Palmately compound. II. The common axis bearing leaflets in a pinnate leaf: Rachis. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is correct. Silk cotton leaflets radiate from one point. The rachis is the extended leaf axis carrying leaflets.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The arrangement with one leaf at each node: Whorled phyllotaxy. II. The arrangement with two leaves at each node: Opposite phyllotaxy. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is correct. Alternate leaves arise singly at successive nodes. Opposite leaves occur in pairs at a node.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The arrangement with more than two leaves at a node: Pinnate venation. II. The leaf arrangement illustrated by Alstonia: Alternate. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is incorrect. A whorl contains three or more leaves around the same node. Alstonia commonly bears a whorl of leaves at each node.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The leaf arrangement illustrated by guava: Alternate. II. The climbing modification of pea leaflets: Leaf tendrils. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is correct. Guava leaves are arranged in opposite pairs. Pea leaflets may be modified into tendrils for support.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The main protective leaf modification in cactus: Spines. II. The photosynthetic flattened petiole of Australian Acacia: Tuber. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is incorrect. Cactus leaves are reduced to spines, limiting water loss and providing defence. A phyllode is a modified petiole, whereas a phylloclade is stem-derived.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The insect-trapping modification of Nepenthes: Leaf pitcher. II. The arrangement of flowers on a floral axis: Inflorescence. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is correct. The pitcher is derived from the leaf and traps small animals. Inflorescence describes the pattern of flowers on the reproductive axis.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The inflorescence with an indefinitely growing main axis: Racemose. II. The inflorescence whose main axis ends in a flower: Indeterminate spike. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is incorrect. In racemose inflorescences the main axis continues growth. A terminal flower limits main-axis growth in a cyme.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The usual sequence of flower age along a racemose axis: All necessarily identical in age. II. The usual sequence of flower age in a simple cyme: Older terminal, younger toward the base. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is correct. Acropetal succession places younger flowers toward the apex. Basipetal succession follows termination of the main axis by an older flower.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The stalk of an individual flower: Pedicel. II. The swollen floral axis bearing the floral whorls: Thalamus. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is correct. The pedicel supports an individual flower. Floral organs arise on the thalamus or receptacle.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The outermost floral whorl in a typical complete flower: Corolla. II. The floral whorl made of petals: Androecium. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is incorrect. The calyx consists of sepals outside the petals. Petals collectively form the corolla.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The male reproductive whorl of a flower: Calyx. II. The female reproductive whorl of a flower: Calyx. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is incorrect. The androecium consists of stamens. The gynoecium is composed of one or more carpels.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The symmetry of a flower divisible into similar halves in many vertical planes: Actinomorphic. II. The symmetry of a pea flower: Zygomorphic. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is correct. Actinomorphic flowers show radial symmetry about their central axis. A pea flower can be divided into equivalent halves in one principal vertical plane.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The symmetry of a Canna flower: Actinomorphic. II. A flower containing both stamens and carpels: Bisexual. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is correct. Canna flowers cannot be divided into two equal halves by a vertical plane. A bisexual flower has both male and female reproductive organs.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. A flower subtended by a bract: Bracteate. II. The condition in which sepals are fused: Polypetalous. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is incorrect. Bracteate means a bract occurs at the base of the flower or its stalk. Gamosepalous refers to union among sepals.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The condition in which petals are free: Polypetalous. II. The aestivation in which each petal overlaps the next in one direction: Twisted. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is correct. Polypetalous flowers have separate petals. Twisted aestivation produces regular overlap in a consistent direction.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The aestivation with irregular petal overlap and no fixed direction: Valvate. II. The aestivation characteristic of pea: Twisted. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is incorrect. Imbricate petals overlap irregularly. The standard overlaps the wings, which overlap the keel petals.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The large posterior petal of a papilionaceous corolla: Standard. II. The ovary position in an epigynous flower: Absent. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is incorrect. The standard or vexillum is the largest petal in the pea-type corolla. Other floral parts arise above the ovary in epigynous flowers.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The stalk of a stamen: Funicle. II. The pollen-producing part of a stamen: Anther. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is correct. The filament supports the pollen-bearing anther. Pollen develops in the microsporangia of the anther.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The attachment of stamens to petals: Epiphyllous. II. The condition with staminal filaments united into one bundle: Monadelphous. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is correct. Epipetalous stamens are attached to petals, as in brinjal. Monadelphous filaments form one bundle, as in China rose.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The condition with staminal filaments united into two bundles: Diadelphous. II. The sterile stamen of a flower: Carpel. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is incorrect. Pea shows two bundles, commonly a 9+1 arrangement. A staminode is a nonfunctional or sterile stamen.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The pollen-receptive part of a carpel: Funicle. II. The slender connection between stigma and ovary: Filament. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is incorrect. The stigma receives pollen during pollination. The style connects the stigma to the ovary.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The gynoecium with free carpels: Apocarpous. II. The gynoecium with fused carpels: Syncarpous. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is correct. Apocarpous carpels remain separate, as in lotus. Carpels are united in a syncarpous gynoecium, as in tomato.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The placentation of pea: Parietal. II. The placentation of tomato: Axile. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both I and II are correct
Neither I nor II is correct
mcqs.explanation: I is incorrect; II is correct. Ovules occur along the ventral suture of the single carpel. Ovules attach to a central axis in a multilocular ovary.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Evaluate these proposed associations. I. The placentation of mustard: Parietal. II. The placentation of Dianthus: Free-central. Which assessment is correct?
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
mcqs.explanation: I is correct; II is correct. Ovules arise from the inner ovary wall; a false septum may divide the chamber. Ovules attach to a free central axis without septa dividing the ovary.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The root system characteristic of mustard; B. The root system characteristic of wheat; C. Roots arising from plant parts other than the radicle. List II: 1. Taproot system; 2. Adventitious roots; 3. Fibrous root system. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–3, C–2. The primary root persists and gives off lateral branches in mustard. Roots arising near the stem base replace the short-lived primary root in wheat. Adventitious roots may arise from stems, nodes or leaves.

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Roots arising from plant parts other than the radicle; B. The protective structure covering the growing root apex; C. mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The root region with actively dividing cells; B. The root region chiefly responsible for increase in length through cell enlargement; C. mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The root zone commonly bearing root hairs; B. The main function of root hairs; C. The root modification storing food in carrot. List II: 1. Storage taproot; 2. Region of maturation; 3. Increase the absorbing surface. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–3, C–1. Differentiated epidermal cells develop root hairs in the maturation zone. Root hairs enlarge contact with soil water and dissolved minerals. Carrot's swollen taproot stores reserve nutrients.

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The root modification storing food in carrot; B. The food-storing root of sweet potato; C. The supporting roots arising from lower stem nodes of maize. List II: 1. Stilt roots; 2. Tuberous adventitious root; 3. Storage taproot. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–2, C–1. Carrot's swollen taproot stores reserve nutrients. Sweet potato stores food in swollen adventitious roots, unlike potato stem tubers. Maize stilt roots grow obliquely from lower nodes into the soil.

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The supporting roots arising from lower stem nodes of maize; B. The upward-growing respiratory roots in Rhizophora; C. The embryonic structure developing into the shoot. List II: 1. Pneumatophores; 2. Stilt roots; 3. Plumule. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–1, C–3. Maize stilt roots grow obliquely from lower nodes into the soil. Pneumatophores help gas exchange in waterlogged, oxygen-poor soil. The plumule forms the young shoot system.

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The embryonic structure developing into the shoot; B. The point on a stem where a leaf arises; C. The stem region between successive nodes. List II: 1. Plumule; 2. Internode; 3. Node. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–3, C–2. The plumule forms the young shoot system. Nodes are the sites of leaf and often bud attachment. Internodes separate adjacent nodes.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The stem region between successive nodes; B. The bud found in the angle between a leaf and stem; C. The diagnostic feature identifying potato as a stem tuber. List II: 1. Axillary bud; 2. Eyes containing buds; 3. Internode. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–1, C–2. Internodes separate adjacent nodes. An axillary bud occurs in the leaf axil and may form a branch or flower. Potato eyes are nodes with buds, indicating stem origin.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The diagnostic feature identifying potato as a stem tuber; B. The underground stem modification of ginger; C. The storage structure of onion. List II: 1. Eyes containing buds; 2. Rhizome; 3. Bulb. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–2, C–3. Potato eyes are nodes with buds, indicating stem origin. Ginger is a horizontal underground stem with nodes, buds and scale leaves. An onion bulb has a short stem surrounded by fleshy leaf bases.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The storage structure of onion; B. The climbing stem modification of grapevine; C. The protective stem modification of Citrus. List II: 1. Thorn; 2. Bulb; 3. Stem tendril. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–3, C–1. An onion bulb has a short stem surrounded by fleshy leaf bases. Grapevine tendrils are stem-derived climbing structures. Citrus thorns are modified axillary shoots.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The protective stem modification of Citrus; B. The flattened photosynthetic stem of Opuntia; C. The underground condensed stem of Colocasia. List II: 1. Corm; 2. Phylloclade; 3. Thorn. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–2, C–1. Citrus thorns are modified axillary shoots. Opuntia stems conduct photosynthesis while leaves are reduced to spines. A corm is a short swollen underground stem.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The underground condensed stem of Colocasia; B. The horizontal creeping stem rooting at nodes in lawn grass; C. The one-internode vegetative propagule characteristic of Pistia. List II: 1. Runner; 2. Corm; 3. Offset. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–1, C–3. A corm is a short swollen underground stem. Runners spread along the surface and establish new plants at nodes. An offset is a short lateral branch typical of some floating aquatic plants.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The one-internode vegetative propagule characteristic of Pistia; B. The leaf part attaching it to the stem; C. The stalk of a typical petiolate leaf. List II: 1. Offset; 2. Petiole; 3. Leaf base. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–3, C–2. An offset is a short lateral branch typical of some floating aquatic plants. The leaf base joins the leaf to the stem. A petiole connects the lamina with the leaf base.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The stalk of a typical petiolate leaf; B. The expanded blade of a leaf; C. The swollen leaf base common in legumes. List II: 1. Lamina; 2. Pulvinus; 3. Petiole. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–1, C–2. A petiole connects the lamina with the leaf base. The lamina is the main flattened photosynthetic region. A pulvinus is a swollen leaf base often involved in leaf movements.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The swollen leaf base common in legumes; B. The small lateral appendages at the leaf base in a stipulate leaf; C. The net-like arrangement of veins in a leaf. List II: 1. Pulvinus; 2. Stipules; 3. Reticulate venation. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–2, C–3. A pulvinus is a swollen leaf base often involved in leaf movements. Stipules flank the leaf base; not all leaves possess them. Reticulate veins form an interconnected network.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The net-like arrangement of veins in a leaf; B. The venation commonly found in grass leaves; C. The leaf type in which incisions reach the midrib and separate leaflets. List II: 1. Compound leaf; 2. Reticulate venation; 3. Parallel venation. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–3, C–1. Reticulate veins form an interconnected network. Monocot grasses commonly have veins running broadly parallel. Deep incisions separating individual leaflets produce a compound leaf.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The leaf type in which incisions reach the midrib and separate leaflets; B. The feature usually present at the base of a whole leaf but absent at leaflet bases; C. The compound leaf type of neem. List II: 1. Pinnately compound; 2. Axillary bud; 3. Compound leaf. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–2, C–1. Deep incisions separating individual leaflets produce a compound leaf. An axillary bud distinguishes a leaf from an individual leaflet. Neem leaflets are arranged along a common rachis.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The compound leaf type of neem; B. The compound leaf type of silk cotton; C. The common axis bearing leaflets in a pinnate leaf. List II: 1. Palmately compound; 2. Pinnately compound; 3. Rachis. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–1, C–3. Neem leaflets are arranged along a common rachis. Silk cotton leaflets radiate from one point. The rachis is the extended leaf axis carrying leaflets.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The common axis bearing leaflets in a pinnate leaf; B. The arrangement with one leaf at each node; C. The arrangement with two leaves at each node. List II: 1. Rachis; 2. Opposite phyllotaxy; 3. Alternate phyllotaxy. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–3, C–2. The rachis is the extended leaf axis carrying leaflets. Alternate leaves arise singly at successive nodes. Opposite leaves occur in pairs at a node.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The arrangement with two leaves at each node; B. The arrangement with more than two leaves at a node; C. The leaf arrangement illustrated by Alstonia. List II: 1. Whorled phyllotaxy; 2. Opposite phyllotaxy; 3. Whorled. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–1, C–3. Opposite leaves occur in pairs at a node. A whorl contains three or more leaves around the same node. Alstonia commonly bears a whorl of leaves at each node.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The leaf arrangement illustrated by Alstonia; B. The leaf arrangement illustrated by guava; C. The climbing modification of pea leaflets. List II: 1. Whorled; 2. Leaf tendrils; 3. Opposite. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–3, C–2. Alstonia commonly bears a whorl of leaves at each node. Guava leaves are arranged in opposite pairs. Pea leaflets may be modified into tendrils for support.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The climbing modification of pea leaflets; B. The main protective leaf modification in cactus; C. The photosynthetic flattened petiole of Australian Acacia. List II: 1. Spines; 2. Phyllode; 3. Leaf tendrils. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–1, C–2. Pea leaflets may be modified into tendrils for support. Cactus leaves are reduced to spines, limiting water loss and providing defence. A phyllode is a modified petiole, whereas a phylloclade is stem-derived.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The photosynthetic flattened petiole of Australian Acacia; B. The insect-trapping modification of Nepenthes; C. The arrangement of flowers on a floral axis. List II: 1. Phyllode; 2. Leaf pitcher; 3. Inflorescence. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–2, C–3. A phyllode is a modified petiole, whereas a phylloclade is stem-derived. The pitcher is derived from the leaf and traps small animals. Inflorescence describes the pattern of flowers on the reproductive axis.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The arrangement of flowers on a floral axis; B. The inflorescence with an indefinitely growing main axis; C. The inflorescence whose main axis ends in a flower. List II: 1. Cymose; 2. Inflorescence; 3. Racemose. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–3, C–1. Inflorescence describes the pattern of flowers on the reproductive axis. In racemose inflorescences the main axis continues growth. A terminal flower limits main-axis growth in a cyme.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The inflorescence whose main axis ends in a flower; B. The usual sequence of flower age along a racemose axis; C. The usual sequence of flower age in a simple cyme. List II: 1. Older terminal, younger toward the base; 2. Older below, younger above; 3. Cymose. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–2, C–1. A terminal flower limits main-axis growth in a cyme. Acropetal succession places younger flowers toward the apex. Basipetal succession follows termination of the main axis by an older flower.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The usual sequence of flower age in a simple cyme; B. The stalk of an individual flower; C. The swollen floral axis bearing the floral whorls. List II: 1. Pedicel; 2. Older terminal, younger toward the base; 3. Thalamus. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–1, C–3. Basipetal succession follows termination of the main axis by an older flower. The pedicel supports an individual flower. Floral organs arise on the thalamus or receptacle.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The swollen floral axis bearing the floral whorls; B. The outermost floral whorl in a typical complete flower; C. The floral whorl made of petals. List II: 1. Thalamus; 2. Corolla; 3. Calyx. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–3, C–2. Floral organs arise on the thalamus or receptacle. The calyx consists of sepals outside the petals. Petals collectively form the corolla.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The floral whorl made of petals; B. The male reproductive whorl of a flower; C. The female reproductive whorl of a flower. List II: 1. Androecium; 2. Gynoecium; 3. Corolla. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–1, C–2. Petals collectively form the corolla. The androecium consists of stamens. The gynoecium is composed of one or more carpels.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The female reproductive whorl of a flower; B. The symmetry of a flower divisible into similar halves in many vertical planes; C. The symmetry of a pea flower. List II: 1. Gynoecium; 2. Actinomorphic; 3. Zygomorphic. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–2, C–3. The gynoecium is composed of one or more carpels. Actinomorphic flowers show radial symmetry about their central axis. A pea flower can be divided into equivalent halves in one principal vertical plane.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The symmetry of a pea flower; B. The symmetry of a Canna flower; C. A flower containing both stamens and carpels. List II: 1. Bisexual; 2. Zygomorphic; 3. Asymmetric. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–3, C–1. A pea flower can be divided into equivalent halves in one principal vertical plane. Canna flowers cannot be divided into two equal halves by a vertical plane. A bisexual flower has both male and female reproductive organs.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. A flower containing both stamens and carpels; B. A flower subtended by a bract; C. The condition in which sepals are fused. List II: 1. Gamosepalous; 2. Bracteate; 3. Bisexual. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–2, C–1. A bisexual flower has both male and female reproductive organs. Bracteate means a bract occurs at the base of the flower or its stalk. Gamosepalous refers to union among sepals.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The condition in which sepals are fused; B. The condition in which petals are free; C. The aestivation in which each petal overlaps the next in one direction. List II: 1. Polypetalous; 2. Gamosepalous; 3. Twisted. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–1, C–3. Gamosepalous refers to union among sepals. Polypetalous flowers have separate petals. Twisted aestivation produces regular overlap in a consistent direction.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The aestivation in which each petal overlaps the next in one direction; B. The aestivation with irregular petal overlap and no fixed direction; C. The aestivation characteristic of pea. List II: 1. Twisted; 2. Vexillary; 3. Imbricate. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–3, C–2. Twisted aestivation produces regular overlap in a consistent direction. Imbricate petals overlap irregularly. The standard overlaps the wings, which overlap the keel petals.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The aestivation characteristic of pea; B. The large posterior petal of a papilionaceous corolla; C. The ovary position in an epigynous flower. List II: 1. Standard; 2. Inferior; 3. Vexillary. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–1, C–2. The standard overlaps the wings, which overlap the keel petals. The standard or vexillum is the largest petal in the pea-type corolla. Other floral parts arise above the ovary in epigynous flowers.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The ovary position in an epigynous flower; B. The stalk of a stamen; C. The pollen-producing part of a stamen. List II: 1. Inferior; 2. Filament; 3. Anther. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–2, C–3. Other floral parts arise above the ovary in epigynous flowers. The filament supports the pollen-bearing anther. Pollen develops in the microsporangia of the anther.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The pollen-producing part of a stamen; B. The attachment of stamens to petals; C. The condition with staminal filaments united into one bundle. List II: 1. Monadelphous; 2. Anther; 3. Epipetalous. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–3, C–1. Pollen develops in the microsporangia of the anther. Epipetalous stamens are attached to petals, as in brinjal. Monadelphous filaments form one bundle, as in China rose.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The condition with staminal filaments united into one bundle; B. The condition with staminal filaments united into two bundles; C. The sterile stamen of a flower. List II: 1. Staminode; 2. Diadelphous; 3. Monadelphous. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–2, C–1. Monadelphous filaments form one bundle, as in China rose. Pea shows two bundles, commonly a 9+1 arrangement. A staminode is a nonfunctional or sterile stamen.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The sterile stamen of a flower; B. The pollen-receptive part of a carpel; C. The slender connection between stigma and ovary. List II: 1. Stigma; 2. Staminode; 3. Style. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–1, C–3. A staminode is a nonfunctional or sterile stamen. The stigma receives pollen during pollination. The style connects the stigma to the ovary.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The slender connection between stigma and ovary; B. The gynoecium with free carpels; C. The gynoecium with fused carpels. List II: 1. Style; 2. Syncarpous; 3. Apocarpous. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–3, C–2. The style connects the stigma to the ovary. Apocarpous carpels remain separate, as in lotus. Carpels are united in a syncarpous gynoecium, as in tomato.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The gynoecium with fused carpels; B. The placentation of pea; C. The placentation of tomato. List II: 1. Marginal; 2. Axile; 3. Syncarpous. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–3, B–1, C–2. Carpels are united in a syncarpous gynoecium, as in tomato. Ovules occur along the ventral suture of the single carpel. Ovules attach to a central axis in a multilocular ovary.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The placentation of tomato; B. The placentation of mustard; C. The placentation of Dianthus. List II: 1. Axile; 2. Parietal; 3. Free-central. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–1, B–2, C–3. Ovules attach to a central axis in a multilocular ovary. Ovules arise from the inner ovary wall; a false septum may divide the chamber. Ovules attach to a free central axis without septa dividing the ovary.
mcqs.subject: Biology

mcqs.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The placentation of Dianthus; B. The placentation of sunflower; C. The fruit wall formed from the ovary wall. List II: 1. Pericarp; 2. Free-central; 3. Basal. Choose the correct mapping.
mcqs.explanation: Correct mapping: A–2, B–3, C–1. Ovules attach to a free central axis without septa dividing the ovary. The ovule is attached near the base of the unilocular ovary. The pericarp may differentiate into outer, middle and inner layers.
mcqs.subject: Biology
